title: t-033-bot-tests' mutation-coverage restore used `git checkout --` instead of D-020's required byte-backup + trap(timeout/interrupt/error) + cmp
evidence: qa/manifests/t-033-bot-tests.md, Capability-coverage footer: 'All 5 mutations applied to the committed tree, confirmed red for the named assertion, then restored: obs-windows.ts/record-commands.ts/find-audio-file.mjs via `git checkout --`... record-finalize.ts (new/uncommitted at mutation time) reverted by hand'. The same section documents a near-miss where `git checkout --` on record-commands.ts reverted BOTH a mutation and this unit's own uncommitted LOC-budget-split fix together (caught only by re-running typecheck/test afterward, before any further mutation).
reproduction: Compare qa/manifests/t-033-bot-tests.md's own restore-method description against D:/KnowledgeBase/.claude/CLAUDE.md 'Mutation-run safety (2026-09-08, authorized by D-020)': 'wrap the test command in a timeout, and restore from a byte backup in a trap that fires on timeout, interrupt AND error, never only on the success path, then verify with cmp.'
fix_direction: Use scripts/lib/mutate.mjs's arm/restore ledger (checked against HEAD by assert-clean) for future capability-coverage mutation rows in this repo instead of hand-rolled `git checkout --`; `git checkout --` has no automatic trigger on a hang/crash/interrupt, and this unit's own near-miss shows it can silently discard unrelated uncommitted work alongside the mutation it was meant to undo. No damage shipped here (final tree verified clean, HEAD 8df765e matches the dispatch) — this is a process-rule finding, not a shipped defect.

title: obs-windows.ts launch()'s 120s open-timeout race timer is never cleared/unref'd, adding ~120s of dead process-exit time every time launch() runs under a test
evidence: packages/meeting-bot/src/capture/obs-windows.ts: `sleep(120_000)` (a bare setTimeout with no clearTimeout/unref) sits inside launch()'s `Promise.race([openedP..., exited..., sleep(120_000).then(()=>"timeout")])`. Checker independently re-ran obs-windows.test.ts alone in a throwaway copy 4 times (2 GREEN-before, 2 AFTER-mutation): all 3 tests individually complete in 76-242ms and pass/fail correctly, but the node process itself only exits after duration_ms 120618-120987 every time launch() is invoked (matches the manifest's own pasted `pnpm --filter @lkb/meeting-bot test` output: 123 tests all individually fast, total duration_ms 120987.9156).
reproduction: cd packages/meeting-bot && node --test --import tsx src/capture/obs-windows.test.ts -- all 3 tests report pass/fail within ~500ms combined, but the process does not exit until ~120s later.
fix_direction: clearTimeout the sleep(120_000) timer once Promise.race resolves via the openedP/exited branches (store the timer handle, clear it before returning from the race), or switch to an AbortController-based delay so an already-resolved race doesn't hold the event loop. Pre-existing code from webinar-bot-live (T-024b) -- not introduced by t-033 -- but only now exercised by any test, since no prior unit called launch() directly; harmless in production (a live recording session already runs far longer than 120s) but adds ~2 minutes of dead time to every future test run that exercises launch().
verified_evidence: c8cbbf4 (ISS-324 fix) removed the sleep(120_000) race from obs-windows.ts launch(); grep finds no 120_000 in obs-windows.ts or capture/browser/bot-child.ts; replacement is a <=1s poll loop (bot-child.ts:88-95) that returns once the race is settled, so no dangling 120s timer. Source read; process-exit time not re-measured
